units.name: Kitchen basics
units.goal: Cuts soft foods safely with a paring knife; uses mitts, turns handles in, and knows a lid goes on a pan fire; reads a recipe through and sets everything out first; measures dry and wet, and halves or doubles a recipe

units.name: No-cook
units.goal: Peels, cores, and seeds produce; makes a dip and a whisked dressing; builds a cold main dish

units.name: Clean meat, poultry, and fish
units.goal: Reads labels for hidden unclean ingredients; handles raw ground beef, ready-cut chicken, and fish with separate boards and clean hands; reads a thermometer (160°F for ground beef, 165°F for chicken, 145°F for fish); stores raw meat on the bottom shelf

units.name: Baking
units.goal: Uses the muffin and biscuit methods, measures flour correctly, makes a simple yeast dough with an adult, and tests doneness with a toothpick

units.name: Boiling, simmering, and steaming
units.goal: Steams vegetables safely; boils eggs soft and hard; cooks white rice by ratio; tells a boil from a simmer and makes a soup from boxed broth; cooks and drains pasta safely

units.name: Stovetop
units.goal: Preheats a pan and tests it; cooks eggs in a pan; sautés vegetables without crowding; browns ground beef and cooks chicken pieces to 165°F; makes a guided white sauce

units.name: Oven and grill
units.goal: Uses the broiler safely; roasts vegetables evenly; roasts chicken to 165°F near the bone; bakes a casserole through

units.name: Low and slow
units.goal: Keeps a pot at a low simmer, stirring and scraping so nothing sticks; shreds cooked chicken; knows when a simmered dish is done. A slow cooker can stand in for the stovetop

units.name: Sabbath capstone
units.goal: Seasons by tasting, tells herbs from spices, and prepares one Sabbath dish from a written prep list
